entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
1. Complainant-petitioner has filed instant transfer petition under section 447 of the BNSS, 2023 with the prayer to transfer the Criminal Case No.146/2023, State Vs. Umakant & Ors., pending before the Court of learned Addl. Chief Judicial Magistrate No.1, Weir, District Bharatpur to jurisdiction of ACJM at Place Bayana or jurisdiction of ACJM at place Bharatpur or ACJM No.2,
Weir and also to quash and set aside the order dated 23.10.2024 passed by the Court of learned Sessions Judge, [2024:RJ-JP:46466] (2 of 3) [CRLTP-86/2024] Bharatpur and further to allow the transfer petition filed by him before the Court of learned District & Sessions Judge, Bharatpur.
2. Counsel for the complainant petitioner submits that the learned trial court wants to decide the case pending before it without collecting the evidence and also without affording sufficient opportunity to the petitioner.

3. On the other hand, the learned Public Prosecutor opposed the submissions advanced by the counsel for the complainant petitioner and supported the order dated 23.10.2024 passed by the Court of learned District & Sessions Judge, Bharatpur.

4. Considered the submissions advanced by the counsel appearing for the complainant petitioner,
learned Public Prosecutor appearing for the State as also the material made available to the Court.
5.

Indisputably, the case pending before the Court of learned Addl. Chief Judicial Magistrate No.1,
Weir, District [2024:RJ-JP:46466] (3 of 3) [CRLTP-86/2024] Bharatpur is at the final stage.

entities.text:
Addl. Chief Judicial Magistrate No.1,
Weir, District [2024:RJ-JP:46466] (3 of 3)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The impugned order dated 23.10.2024 passed by the Court of learned District & Sessions Judge,
Bharatpur, reflects that whatever the allegations the complainant petitioner levelled allegations against the concerned Presiding Officer in the application filed by her, the arguing counsel during the course of argument admitted be bald and baseless which resulted into withdrawal of the said application.
However, the complainant petitioner failed to prove any of the specific allegations levelled against the concerned Presiding Officer.

The finding given by the court below that if on such baseless allegations the matters are transferred then it is not possible for the Judicial Officers to work properly, is just and proper and warrant no interference of this Court and more particularly when the case is posted for final hearing & disposal.
6. The transfer petition filed by the complainant petitioner is based on baseless allegations, lacs merit and accordingly stands dismissed.
(GANESH RAM MEENA),J NK Sharma/Dy.
